title: Capacity stitching checklist and ops notes - GPU regional handoff
content:
Weekly capacity stitching notes (short, messy) - primary focus: regional GPU handoff cadence + quick checklist for oncall/sprint swap

Context:
- We experimented with staggered priming in APAC + EU this past week to smooth cross-region tail latency during morning surges. Mixed signals: cost up ~5% but 95p latency improved in EU by ~18ms for customer-tiered traffic.
- This doc is a working checklist to use during shift handoffs and a capture of observations, hypotheses, and follow-ups. Keep concise when handing off.

1) Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Current regional buffer targets: APAC 18% spare, EU 14%, NA 10% (adjusted after Friday simulation).
- Short-term action: keep APAC priming cadence at +2 warmups per hour overnight for next 48h; evaluate day 3.
- Longer-term: prototype opportunistic backfill with lower-priority pooled jobs (see RFC link).

2) Observations from priming run (2029-07-27 -> 2029-07-29):
- APAC: prefix cache hit rate rose from 62% -> 74% after adding two warmers; token cost increased ~4.8% but effective user-facing latency drop notable for short queries (<120 tokens).
- EU: saw burst preemption incidents 2029-07-28 03:10Z (2 nodes); root cause likely cloud provider maintenance overlap + preemption config mismatch on lower-tier pool.
- NA: stable, but queueing increased for large-batch embeddings window 09:00-11:00 PT. Might need burst lane increase.
- Note: weird metric blip in metrics.gpu_util.avg where value fell 0.15 at 2029-07-28 02:00Z for 7m — correlates with autoscaler throttle.

3) Handoff checklist (for next shift / oncall):
- [ ] Check priming-run status dashboard: /dashboards/priming-cadence (quick look at prefix hit and warmers active).
- [ ] Confirm APAC warmers count == requested (target: +2 overnight). If not, escalate to Arjun (pager INFRA-priming).
- [ ] Verify EU preemption guardrails: preemption-weight tag present on lower-tier pools. If missing, follow remediation steps in runbook.
- [ ] Review recent autoscaler throttles: query metrics.autoscaler.throttles.last24h and capture anomalies.
- [ ] Leave short note in #gpu-ops: "handoff: priming=APAC+2, EU watchlist, NA embedding-burst".
- [ ] If >1 preemption incidents in 30m, trigger cross-region fallback (runbook step 4) and notify SRE.

4) Immediate action items (owner, due):
- Priya: run retrospective parse on prefix hit vs token-cost delta (due 2029-08-02).
- Luis: convert the ad-hoc priming experiment into a scheduled job in k8s (job template + config) (due 2029-08-05).
- Hannah: add an alert for autoscaler throttle frequency > 3/hour (alert ID: INFRA-AUTO-89) (due 2029-07-31).
- Arjun: patch preemption-tag mismatch for EU lower-tier pool and validate in smoke test (due 2029-07-31).

5) Hypotheses to validate (quick):
- H1: Short-query latency improves because KV-cache hit synergy increases with frequent warmers; cost increase is mostly fixed overhead. Test: run A/B with warmers disabled for subset traffic and capture 95p lat + token cost.
- H2: Autoscaler throttles are caused by competing scheduler locks during heavy rollout windows (e.g., model rollout at 02:00Z). Test: coordinate a quiet window and reobserve.

6) Telemetry snippets / queries to run during handoff (copy to stack):
- prefix_hit = SELECT avg(hit_rate) FROM metrics.prefix_cache WHERE region in ("EU","APAC") AND window=6h;
- autoscaler_throttle = SELECT count(*) FROM metrics.autoscaler where label="throttle" AND window=24h;
- preemptions = SELECT count(*) FROM events.preemption WHERE region="eu-west-1" AND window=48h;
- note: if preemptions > 2 -> follow runbook step 4.

7) Runbook gaps (add to backlog):
- Missing playbook entry for "opportunistic backfill" – needs runbook steps + SLA notes. (backlog: INFRA-1745)
- No standard for measuring incremental cost per priming-warmup; need small accounting job keyed by job-id.
- Clarify fallback model variant mapping when region falls below buffer threshold (currently fuzzy).

8) Cost / performance sketch (rough numbers, do not publish):
- Baseline token cost (global) = $X per M tokens (we'll fill in with finance numbers).
- Current week priming incremental = ~+5% cost in APAC, but saves estimated 12k 95p-ms-seconds customer latency (converted to x dollars? TBD).
- If priming is left at +2 warmers for 7 days -> estimated extra spend = ~0.9% monthly.

9) Notes to self / messy bits:
- We didn't capture request-level bucket for short vs long queries cleanly; fix tagging in ingestion to better segment.
- Luis mentioned an upgrade to the prewarming controller that could reduce warmup cost by ~10% — follow up with PR review.
- Keep watch on Friday scheduled maintenance windows in EU; they overlap with our low-cost pool maintenance and cause preemptions.

10) Retrospective items for next sync (agenda items):
- Quick review of priming A/B results (5m)
- Autoscaler throttle spike root cause theory (10m)
- Backfill strategy proposal review (10m)
- Ops runbook cleanup assignment (5m)

11) Slack / meeting links (quick):
- Slack thread: #gpu-ops "priming-run-2029-07-27" (search in Slack)
- Meeting: infra-ops-standup 2029-07-31 notes (call link on calendar)

12) Unresolved questions (capture):
- How do we quantify user impact of 18ms 95p improvement? Product team needs guidance; pinged @product-ux for signal.
- Can finance accept a temporary 1% bump in monthly spend for improved latency? Open: finance sync next Tues.

---
If you're taking over oncall: keep this doc brief in your handoff message and mark items done inline. If anything looks flaky, call Arjun first (he has regional infra keys) and Luis for priming job ops.

End of notes.
